$description: VoxClip design tokens. Source of truth for both apps. Generated outputs: apps/macos/Sources/VoxClip/Design/Tokens.swift, apps/windows/src/VoxClip.App/Themes/Tokens.xaml and apps/macos/Resources/Assets.xcassets/AccentColor.colorset/Contents.json (tools/design). Spec: doc/design.md section 16.

conventions.syntax: W3C Design Tokens group/token syntax ($type, $value, $description). Colour tokens are the exception: $value is a mode map {dark, light}.
conventions.system: A value of the form system:<name> means the platform colour named in $extensions.com.voxconvo.voxclip.macos / .windows; the generator must not substitute a hex value.
conventions.highContrast: windowsHighContrast names the WinUI SystemColor* resource used in the HighContrast theme dictionary. macOS relies on Increase Contrast and the system colours.
conventions.units: Lengths are points on macOS and effective pixels (epx) on Windows. Durations are milliseconds.
conventions.platformValues: A dimension's $value is the macOS value; $extensions.com.voxconvo.voxclip.windows replaces it in Tokens.xaml only.
conventions.macosAsset: A colour whose extensions name macosAsset is also generated as apps/macos/Resources/Assets.xcassets/<name>.colorset (light for Any, dark for Dark).
conventions.source: Names the design-study token a colour's value comes from (Document <name>, or ADR-R29 <mockup name>).

window.$description: Behind content and sheets; same values as bg.sunken. On macOS system chrome draws its own glass over it. Windows: Mica shows through instead; use only as the Mica fallback colour.

surface.$description: Transcript page and other long-reading content surfaces.

sunken.$description: Preview dock, timeline bed, Welcome side pane, empty-state cards.

elevated.$description: Caption tiles, popover fallback, onboarding cards, callout base.

muted.$description: Hover and pressed rows, skeleton bars, tile placeholders.

input.$description: Custom input backgrounds only. System text fields keep their own fill.

default.$description: Hairline dividers (clip rows, inspector sections). Decorative, so exempt from the 3:1 boundary minimum.

strong.$description: Control boundaries, and borders on custom surfaces under Reduce Transparency / Increase Contrast. At least 3:1 against bg.surface, bg.sunken and bg.window.

primary.$description: Body and transcript text. Contrast on bg.surface: dark 14.2:1, light 16.3:1.

muted.$description: Helper text, clip reasons, pause token text. Between text.secondary and text.tertiary, so the hierarchy stays monotonic; the study's pauseFg (#B0B2B8 / #55585F) was brighter than text.secondary. Contrast on pause.background: dark 5.28:1, light 5.16:1.

tertiary.$description: Gutter timecodes, footnotes, mono caps status labels. The lightest text step: still 4.5:1 on bg.surface, bg.sunken and bg.elevated.

disabled.$description: Disabled labels only (exempt from contrast minimums).

default.$description: Petrol, the one accent, as a fill that carries text: prominent buttons, the selected choice, the playing word. The macOS AccentColor asset is generated from this token. On Windows App.xaml sets it as SystemAccentColorDark1 (light) and SystemAccentColor (dark). accent.on on it: light 5.9:1, dark 4.65:1.

pressed.$description: Pressed state of accent.default fills. Windows light SystemAccentColorDark2.

text.$description: Petrol as text and marks on page, sunken and glass surfaces: links, rings, clip brackets and badges, the playhead, info icons. macOS DesignValues.accentText uses it while the system accent is the AccentColor asset and follows controlAccentColor otherwise. Windows dark SystemAccentColorLight2.

on.$description: Text and glyphs on accent.default and accent.pressed, matching the macOS system white on the accent. Contrast on accent.default: light 5.9:1, dark 4.65:1. Windows draws TextOnAccentFillColorPrimary from App.xaml instead.

soft.$description: Custom selection tint and the drop-target veil base. text.primary on it: light 13.3:1, dark 9.5:1.

text.$description: Platform text selection: the macOS transcript and text fields on both platforms. Always the platform selection colour, which follows the Petrol accent ramp.

transcript.$description: Windows transcript selection, drawn by the app with text.primary on it (dark 7.96:1, light 11.5:1). The same values macOS derives from the Petrol accent; never the playing-word fill. In High Contrast it is Highlight, so selected words use HighlightText.

playingBackground.$description: Fill behind the currently playing word (radius.xs, 2 pt inline padding): the accent fill.

playingForeground.$description: Text of the playing word. Contrast light 5.9:1, dark 4.65:1.

cut.$description: Text of cut words (still content, kept at >= 4.5:1). Also on pause.background behind a cut word that matches a search, so a step past the study's cutText: dark 5.7:1 on bg.surface and 4.73:1 on pause.background, light 5.28:1 and 4.62:1.

filler.$description: Suggested-filler dotted underline (macOS) and filler word text (Windows). Contrast on bg.surface: dark 8.4:1, light 5.2:1.

lowConfidence.$description: Dashed underline for low-confidence words (off by default).

correctionDot.$description: 2 pt dot under the first letter of a corrected word.

stroke.$description: Strikethrough line on cut words (macOS; Windows strikes in word.cut because XAML text decorations use the foreground). Contrast on bg.surface: dark 6.4:1, light 4.9:1.

fill.$description: Timeline hatch stripes for cut word ranges (2 pt stripes every 6 pt at 45 degrees). Contrast on timeline.track: dark 5.6:1, light 4.0:1.

pauseFill.$description: Timeline hatch stripes for cut pause ranges.

background.$description: Inline pause token and the collapsed '... 5 cut' token. Token text uses text.muted (dark 5.28:1, light 5.16:1).

warning.$description: Warning icons and text, slow states. Suggested fillers use word.filler.

warningBackground.$description: Custom warning callouts; Windows uses InfoBar severity colours instead.

dangerBackground.$description: Custom error rows and callouts; Windows uses InfoBar severity colours instead.

success.$description: Success icons and text. Always pair it with a symbol and words: its hue is close to Petrol.

successBackground.$description: Custom success callouts; Windows uses InfoBar severity colours instead.

infoBackground.$description: Custom informational callouts; the info icon uses accent.text.

badgeBackground.$description: Neutral clip badge fill on the sidebar glass, bg.surface and bg.sunken: paper at 10% (dark), ink at 9% (light). Its numeral is text.secondary, at least 4.5:1 on all three; dark is 10% rather than the delta's 13%, which measures 4.2:1 on the sidebar glass. The selected clip's badge is the accent fill instead.

track.$description: Track drawn on the bg.sunken timeline bed.

keptBackground.$description: Bed behind kept-speech waveforms on the track: paper at 9% (dark), ink at 7% (light).

waveform.$description: RMS waveform bars over kept speech (50 ms buckets, 2 px bars on a 3 px pitch): paper at 58% (dark), ink at 52% (light). At least 3:1 on timeline.keptBackground.

scopeDim.$description: Dims the track outside the selected clip: bg.sunken at 62% (dark), 66% (light). Off in High Contrast, where the brackets and trim handles mark the scope.

clipBracket.$description: The selected clip's 2 pt bracket line and end ticks above the track (accent.text). Unselected clips use line.strong; suggestions are dashed.

clipBand.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout. Band behind the active clip range: accent.default at 12%. Clip scope is now timeline.scopeDim.

stage.$description: Video surround in both appearances and in High Contrast. The only pure black allowed.

foreground.$description: Text and glyphs over video and the stage (transport pill, empty-stage label). The stage and its overlays stay dark in both appearances.

scrim.$description: REC pill and other chips drawn over video (78%).

transportOpaque.$description: Transport pill fill under Reduce Transparency (92%), with line.strong border.

drop.$description: 'Drop to transcribe' overlay background: bg.surface at 92%.

dropBorder.$description: 2 pt dashed border of the drop overlay (accent.text).

dropZoneBorder.$description: 2 pt dashed border of the Welcome drop zone: text.primary at 40%. Decorative; the zone's icon and label identify it.

ring.$description: Custom-drawn focus rings only (2 pt, offset 2), in accent.text. System controls keep the system ring / focus visual.

status.$description: Mono caps status labels (READY TO REVIEW style), gutter labels.

transcript.$description: Transcript page in the system font (SF Pro; Windows Segoe UI Variable Text) at 19/32 on both platforms. Zoom 13-28 pt (macOS) / 13-28 epx (Windows) in steps of 1; line height = size x 32/19.

timecode.$description: Gutter timecodes and timeline labels, m:ss.d.

fontFiles.$description: Brand fonts for rendered video only (captions and the AI MODIFIED label) under ADR-R29: the UI uses system fonts, and the apps stop loading these for UI with the old layout. Files live in shared/fonts/<family>/ with entries in shared/fonts/fonts.json, added through tools/captions/font-sources.json like the caption fonts. 'present' records whether the file is bundled as of 2026-10-25. Until a file is present the apps use the platform fallback named here, so nothing depends on a missing file.

xs.$description: Badges, chips and the playing-word fill.

control.$description: Buttons, the timeline track and the cut pause chip.

pane.$description: The video stage, sidebar selection, the selection bar, cards, thumbnails and callouts.

sheet.$description: Sheets and the whole-window drop overlay.

sm.$description: Pause and collapsed-cut tokens, keycaps, number badges.

lg.$description: Video stage, caption tiles. macOS 26: .containerConcentric with this as fallback.

hatchStripe.$description: Stripe width; stripe period 6, angle 45 degrees.

durationFast.$description: Strike draw-in, Pop caption preview, selection fill.

transportFadeDelay.$description: Transport pill fades after this much playback without pointer over the video (never under Reduce Motion).

spring.$description: SwiftUI .spring(response:dampingFraction:). Windows uses easeOut over durationSlow.

reduceMotion.$description: Every UI animation becomes instant under Reduce Motion (macOS accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion, Windows UISettings.AnimationsEnabled == false). Export output is unaffected.

transcriptMeasureMax.$description: About 72 characters at the default size.

sidebar.$description: Sidebar width: resizable 220-320 on macOS, NavigationView OpenPaneLength 264 on Windows.

rightColumn.$description: Right column (viewer, captions, Rewrite). Default width = ideal - (1440 - window width) x 0.25 within min-max: 360 at 1440 and 320 at 1280 on macOS, 388 and 348 on Windows.

stagePortraitMax.$description: Largest 9:16 stage on both platforms; 1:1 is at most 320 high. The caption gallery scrolls below it.

inspector.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout.

timelineTrackHeight.$description: The whole track height is the scrub target.

selectionBarHeight.$description: Transcript selection bar: 36 (macOS glass bar), 40 (Windows CommandBarFlyout).

footerStatusHeightWindows.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout.

transportPillHeight.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout.

captionTileAspect.$description: Caption gallery tile height over width. Two tiles per row: width = (column - 8) / 2, height = width x 0.45.

welcomeWindow.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout.

breakpointThreeColumn.$description: deprecated by ADR-R29; removed with the old layout. Window width at or above which the inspector shows by default.

breakpointStack.$description: Below this width the preview stacks above the transcript (max 40% of the window height).
